Check digit11BCheck digit is a data validation method commonly used for numeric data, such as identity number, book number, credit card number, etc.The check digit is generated by a specific algorithm and appended to the end of the numeric data. It can consist of more than one digit.

Parity check12BData is stored in computers as binary codes. Binary code consists of 0 and 1 only.A parity bit can be appended to the end of the binary code to ensure that the total number of 1s in the code is even or odd. This is called a parity check.There are two types of parity checks.Original binary codeTotal number of 1sThe binary code after adding the parity bitEven parity checkOdd parity check0000 00000000 00000000 00011010 10141010 10101010 1011

Data verification18CData verification helps us determine whether the data is accurate and consistent when being transferred between media. Different types of data verification include:TypeDescriptionInputting data twiceIt requires an operator to input the same data twice.Double data entryIt requires two operators to input the same data independently.Proofreading dataIt requires another operator to compare the input data against the original document.

Functions of Database222.3Do you know how a huge amount of data (e.g. book data in a library) is organised, stored and retrieved? The processes are done using database.

Organisation23AThe data in a database is organised according to the database structure. A good database structure enables a better communication between different tables and reduces data redundancy.For example:Field nameData typeDescriptionSIDStringThe unique student ID of a student. A number cannot have leading zeros, thus it has to be stored as text.NAMEStringThe name of a student.SEXStringThe sex of a student.CLASSStringThe class that a student belongs to.CNOIntegerThe class number of a student.

Retrieval26CWe can index frequently accessed fields to speed up the data retrieval process.Indexing ENAME creates an index table containing the indexed field and a pointer to the related records only.
File Access Method272.4Data can be stored in different storage devices. The storage devices determine how data is accessed. There are two common file access methods:

Sequential access28AFor a storage device using sequential access, data is written or accessed sequentially, starting from the beginning. Averagely, it is slower than that of direct access.Storage devices that use sequential access only include: Magnetic tape

Direct access29BFor a storage device using direct access, data can be written in any storage position. The access speed of direct access is more stable and generally faster than that of sequential access.Storage devices that use direct access include: Hard diskUSB flash drive
Data Hierarchy32.1Data is usually stored in a hierarchical form. In a data hierarchy, every higher level of data is a collection of the items from the lower level.

Data Control42.2Data control is the process of managing data. It includes:Data validationData verification

Garbage in, garbage out5A “Garbage in, garbage out”  means that when unreliable or incoherent data is input to a data analysis, the output information will not be useful. Data input errors include:ErrorDescriptionExampleData source errorIncorrect data is provided by data source.Someone provides an email address which does not exist.Transcription errordata is misread, misheard, or mistyped.A typesetter mistyped “冶” as “治”.Transposition errorIncorrect placement of the data.Someone accidentally reverses two adjacent digits when recording a transaction, making “$15” become “$51”
Data validation6BData validation ensures that the input data is reasonable and matches certain rules. It is usually run by systems or programs and widely used in online forms.

Data validation7BTypes of data validation include:TypeFunctionExamplePresence checkIt ensures that there must be data in the required fields.An applicant must provide their name.Fixed value checkIt ensures that the data can only be selected from a list of specific values.The sex of an applicant must be either “M” or “F”.Type checkIt ensures that the data must be of a certain type.The age of an applicant must be a number.Range checkIt ensures that the data must be within a certain range.The age of an applicant must be larger than 12.Length checkIt ensures that the length of the data must match certain criteria.An applicant must provide an 8-digit phone number.Format checkIt ensures that the data must be in a specific format.The email address of an applicant must contain an "@" symbol.

Data validation8BThere are different user interface designs to make data validation easier.TypeData validationExampleDrop-down listFixed value check: only one of the specific values can be input.Radio buttonFixed value check: only one of the specific values can be input.CheckboxesFixed value check: only the specific values can be input. Multiple values can be selected.Date pickerType check: only dates can be input. Invalid dates, like “32/08/2025” cannot be picked.Format check: the date must be in a certain format, such as “DD/MM/YYYY”.
Type check9BTo facilitate data organisation and data analysis, data of the same field should share the same data type.
